title: Marico Ltd - 531642 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Marico Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 13%, EBITDA up 27% to 18.2% margin; FY27 EBITDA growth guidance raised to mid-20s from ~20%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% with India volume up 10% and international up 13% in constant currency, while EBITDA rose 27% and PAT 31%. Gross margin expanded about 600 bps on mix, new growth engines and softer copra, and EBITDA margin still rose 200 bps to 18.2% despite A&P up 44%. Management raised FY27 guidance: teens revenue growth with revenue comfortably above INR15,000 crore, EBITDA growth in the mid-20s (24-25% minimum), and India volume growth in double digits. It also pulled the INR20,000 crore revenue ambition forward from FY30 to FY29, described as an aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: H1 FY27 PAT +28%; highest profit growth in last 50 quarters

segments.name: Parachute (India)
segments.commentary: Volume up 13%, highest in 22 quarters; volume market share gain ~570 bps to a new high of 60%; positive value growth despite deflation after one price cut on loyalty packs.

segments.name: Value-Added Hair Oil (VAHO)
segments.commentary: Value growth 21% for sixth straight quarter; value market share +80 bps (MAT); mid-teens volume growth in mid and premium segments.

segments.name: Saffola Edible Oil
segments.commentary: High single-digit volume decline from rationalising low-margin variants; revenue up 6%; reset to complete over next 2-3 quarters; premium cold-pressed and Saffola Total growing faster.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue up 45%; Saffola Foods early-teens growth led by oats, muesli and soya chunks; True Elements, 4700BC and Cosmix scaling, growth accelerating sequentially.

segments.name: Premium Personal Care
segments.commentary: Portfolio (premium hair nourishment, hair cleansing, male grooming, skin care) above INR500 crore ARR; shampoo expected to cross INR100 crore ARR this year.

segments.name: Digital-first brands (Beardo)
segments.commentary: Beardo scaled over 6x since 2020, expected to cross INR400 crore this year; profitability up 1,900 bps.

segments.name: International Business
segments.commentary: Constant currency growth 13%: Bangladesh +5% (sequential improvement), Vietnam +22%, MENA +15%, South Africa +15%, New Country Development and Exports +17%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth: teens, with revenue comfortably crossing INR15,000 crore and an opportunity to push toward mid-teens.
FY27 EBITDA growth raised to mid-20s (about 24-25% minimum) from ~20% earlier; FY27 EBITDA margin up about 120-150 bps.
FY27 India volume growth expected to touch double digits.
FY28 and FY29 EBITDA growth guided at least mid-teens; FY29 revenue CAGR of about 13-14% cited as achievable.
INR20,000 crore revenue ambition pulled forward from FY30 to FY29 as an aspiration; management says it is organic and any inorganic addition would be upside.

Construct: India high single-digit growth as base case, international mid-teens, inflation about 3%; growth portfolio 20-25%; Parachute mid-single-digit and Saffola medium-term growth; VAHO double-digit value growth.
A&P at about 10-10.5% of ASR next year; India A&P to grow double digits on a steady-state basis.
capex_capacity: SETU 2.0 launched in India, focused on AI and tech-led GTM expansion of premium core and digital brands; SETU rolled out in Vietnam and starting in Bangladesh this quarter.
Direct reach up more than 1.5x; rural stockists nearly doubled (about 1.8x cited later); first phase of SETU estimated ~70% complete.
Almond hair oil to reach INR100 crore+ annualized run rate by FY28; INR200-250 crore ARR by FY30 aspiration.
Shampoo: launched May (this year), expected to cross INR100 crore ARR this year; medium-term INR400-500 crore ARR aspiration.
Beardo expected to cross INR400 crore this year; 4700BC breakeven expected well ahead of target; definitive run rate for Cosmix and 4700BC to be shared by end of next quarter.
demand_pricing: Parachute gained from one price cut targeted at loyalty packs, reversing down-trading; pipeline with distributors among the thinnest in industry; benefit from weaker competitor activity and packaging/gas supply shocks hitting smaller players.
Copra prices about 35% below last year's peak and rangebound; crude-linked derivatives and vegetable oils rose further on geopolitical and weather factors.
Management says demand is resilient in India; watch for deficient rainfall in some states and high crude-driven inflation.
Bangladesh facing demand softness from persistent inflation; growth expected to improve sequentially as it laps high base.
Management said consumer inflation rose led by food, edible oil and fuel.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY27 EBITDA upgrade when copra is stable and non-coconut inflation is higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of favourable portfolio mix from pruning unprofitable lines, procurement advantage, Parachute deflation execution with one price cut, profitability gains in diversification brands, and better visibility into the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the upgrade in FY27 EBITDA a margin normalisation pulled forward, so does FY28 change?
qa_highlights.answer: Pawan Agrawal said the upgrade is for FY27 only; FY28 and FY29 guidance of mid-teens EBITDA growth is unchanged. FY27 margin expansion of 120-150 bps is expected.

qa_highlights.question: How will A&P trend (ad-to-sales ratio)?
qa_highlights.answer: Ad-to-sales to rise marginally and stay at that level; about 10-10.5% of ASR visible for next year. India A&P to grow double digits steady state, after higher FY27 spends on shampoo and almond.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR20,000 crore target inclusive of acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is organic; any inorganic addition is upside. Management says it does not pay 6x for digital brands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on Cosmix and 4700BC post-acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are tracking ahead of acquisition assumptions; Cosmix has high-teens operating margins and will move into VMS; 4700BC breakeven significantly ahead of target, with gifting and quick commerce helping.

qa_highlights.question: Is Just Herbs back on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration issues in year one have been addressed through SKU rationalisation, channel focus and content investment; breakeven expected over the next few quarters.

risks_watch: Crude-linked and vegetable oil inflation could offset softer copra; management says pricing power and cost programme will cushion.
Saffola Edible Oil volume decline (high single digit) during reset over next 2-3 quarters.
Bangladesh growth recovery depends on sequential improvement and SETU rollout.
Deficient rainfall in some Indian states could weigh on demand.
Parachute outperformance partly attributed to transient factors; management expects a deflation-cycle playbook to sustain volumes.
Ambitious INR20,000 crore FY29 target is an aspiration without a bottom-up build yet; SETU 2.0 and shampoo ramp to be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on upgraded FY27 guidance, while explicitly cautious on crude, vegetable oil inflation, rainfall and geopolitical black swans. Management was clear that FY29 revenue target is an aspiration rather than a bottom-up commitment and was less specific on margin percentages.
key_quotes: We are confident to deliver mid-twenties EBITDA growth up from around 20% that we had estimated earlier as we now have better visibility of the full year picture.
We're fully aware that the biggest enemy that stalls a virtuous cycle of growth is management complacency overconfidence and arrogance.
And if you look at it, we must be one of the very few companies which hasn't cut back on A&P in any cycle.
So overall, we see protein by participating with multiple brands, multiple categories, we believe to be a broad-spectrum protein player and will be a big protein player over the medium term.
Now whether it sort of increases the guidance for FY28, not really, we are saying for FY28 or '29 we stick by our guidance of mid-teens growth.

growth.why: FY27 guidance raised: teens revenue growth (comfortably above INR15,000 crore, pushing to mid-teens) and mid-20s EBITDA growth (24-25% minimum), backed by Parachute share gains (volume +13%), VAHO value +21%, Foods +45% and mix/copra tailwinds, but no specific capacity additions or order book numbers were given.
